By the looks of it conda pulls astropy from an `anaconda`
repository and they changed the version, which used to include
`pytest` as a dependency. They no longer do, causing our test
environment to not install pytest through conda and instead
fell back to the system version of pytest.

recommendation from conda at

message:
implement numpy prod workaround

autograd has not yet implemented `np.prod`, so attempts to
use `np.prod(*images)` in `fft_convolve` when one or more of the
images are `ArrayBox`es, the autograd wrapper for arrays used in
gradient calculations, results in an error. This ticket checks
for an `ArrayBox` in `images` and uses a python loop to calculate
the product if one is present.

Create tests for observation.py

While creating the tests a few inconsistencies/sloppy coding were
fixed:
- `Scene.psfs` is now always 3D, even the `target_psf` for the
  model scene. This makes the API more uniform for `Scene`
  and its inherited classes.
- PSF matching and convolutions now use real FFTs. This has the
  advantage that it runs faster, fixes a potential bug in the
  PSF matching code, and is more similar to the `scipy.signal.convolve`
  method.

Add pytorch and FFT convolutions and translations

Anticipating the upgrade to pytorch to make use of autograd,
we implement FFT to perform PSF convolutions and translations
by fractional amounts. This is not implemented in scarlet yet
but exists in the subdirectory `torch`.

The `torch/utils.py` module contains numpy functionality that is
currently not ported to pytorch yet. The `torch/filters.py` module
contains code to perform FFT convolutions using various sinc
approximations. If we end up using a numpy autograd function or
tensorflow then a new file `filters.py` should be created in either
a `numpy` or `tensorflow` directory with the same API.

author: fred3m <fredem@princeton.edu>
message:
Check for odd rows/columns in build_monotonic

When this operator is built for an image with an even number of
rows and/or columns, the result is a catastrophic failure.
This commit adds a check that the user has already projected
the image to a space with an odd number of rows and columns.

It also changes the name of the proximal operator, which
will be useful in the future when implementing a version
of monotonicity that doesn't just look at the radial
direction, but at all directions coming from the peak.
This future change may help model spiral galaxies
more accurately.

ADAM and FISTA is the iteration over the proximal operators in
each iteration of the fit. So changing this to 1 or 2

effect on the overall results.

to prevent the user from having to do so.

* spectrum.py - contains get_best_fit_seds, get_pixel_sed, get_psf_sed from initialization.py
* morphology.py - contains `trim_morphology` and will also include some of the functionality from `init_extended_source` and `init_starlet_source`

* initialization.py - contains `init_extended_source`,  `init_starlet_source`, `init_multicomponent_source` and all of the init functions needed for the testing (`hasEdgeFlux`, `initAllSources`, `iniSource`)
